verdict.rationale: Proa components are written in typed Rust, with markup in compile-time-validated template macros (including raw-string md! templates) and ordinary stylesheets, so a Rust developer reuses familiar language syntax and CSS. The evidence never shows that the template markup is plain standard HTML, and the framework adds its own concepts (signals, islands, RSJS, WebContext, Suspense boundaries), so the learning curve is only partly minimized. Missing for 10: explicit evidence that templates use standard HTML syntax, evidence that a developer can write components with few framework-specific concepts, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the learning curve.

support.subject: As a developer, I can write components using standard markup, styling, and language syntax I already know, minimizing new concepts to learn
